title: Troubleshooting Gurgling Drains and Trap Siphons
description: When a plumbing fixture gurgles or smells like sewer gas after draining, poor ventilation is often the main cause. Without adequate airflow, water moving through the drain creates negative pressure that pulls the water seal out of nearby P-traps. Troubleshooting requires checking roof vent terminals for obstructions like leaves, bird nests, or ice buildup. In systems utilizing Air Admittance Valves (AAVs), a worn or stuck mechanical diaphragm can prevent air intake. Clearing vent blockages or replacing a faulty valve restores pressure balance in the DWV system, protecting trap seals and eliminating gurgling noises.

Troubleshooting Gurgling Drains and Trap Siphons

When a plumbing fixture gurgles or smells like sewer gas after draining, poor ventilation is often the main cause. Without adequate airflow, water moving through the drain creates negative pressure that pulls the water seal out of nearby P-traps. Troubleshooting requires checking roof vent terminals for obstructions like leaves, bird nests, or ice buildup. In systems utilizing Air Admittance Valves (AAVs), a worn or stuck mechanical diaphragm can prevent air intake. Clearing vent blockages or replacing a faulty valve restores pressure balance in the DWV system, protecting trap seals and eliminating gurgling noises.
